baseline.scope: Actual Linux source Electron UI, CodeMirror edits, renderer draftWriter, preload/IPC and real private recovery files. Receiver saveDraft acknowledgements/writes are deliberately gated during the stress phase, then released FIFO; this is a controlled slow bridge, not measured physical-disk latency. 100 ms requested procfs/main-heap observations, no debugger or forced GC; sampled peaks are not continuous peaks. perf_hooks GC entries describe only observed main-process GC events, not renderer or exact stop-the-world pauses. Navigation to blank tears down the old renderer document; final data must already have crossed IPC. No user profile, agents, GPU/model or native Windows/macOS/installer verification.

method: Three fresh serial Linux Electron pairs per workload, middle pair order reversed. Actual editor changes pause 450 ms between revisions against a controlled stalled saveDraft bridge. Requested 100 ms main-heap/procfs observations and main perf_hooks GC entries; no renderer debugger, forced GC, builds, tests or other agent-run benchmarks during the twelve cases. All accepted process-tree samples are complete; rejected attempts are retained. Sampled maxima and descriptive medians are not continuous peaks, randomization or general latency inference.
scope: Bound is per renderer draft writer, not a global byte/app/project cap. Typing permits one active call plus the latest pending source; pagehide/disposal urgently sends the last full snapshot behind that call so document destruction cannot strand it. Host recovery saves are synchronous full replacements; fixture releases gated calls FIFO before validating actual persisted/reopened data. Natural main GC event durations are not exact STW pauses or renderer GC. No GPU, real model, physical disk latency, installed Windows/macOS, general speedup or overall bounded-memory claim.
